name: Suhaym ibn Wathil
bio: Suhaym ibn Wathil belonged to Riyah, a branch of Yarbu' within Tamim, and lived on both sides of the coming of Islam. A man of standing in his tribe, he held a contest in boasting with Ghalib ibn Sa'sa'a, father of the poet al-Farazdaq. Al-Asma'i opens his anthology with Suhaym’s answer to two younger poets, in which he takes the part of the fully grown camel. Al-Zirikli reports Ibn Durayd’s reckoning of forty years in pre-Islamic times and sixty in Islam, and places his death around 60 AH (680 CE).
